newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-HUSSEY GUIDES WESTERN AUSTRALIA TO TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HUSSEY GUIDES WESTERN AUSTRALIA TO TOP.

text.p: Opener Mike Hussey helped Western Australia move six points clear at the top of the Sheffield Shield table by guiding them to victory against Tasmania on Monday.
Hussey added to his first innings 83 with a patient 87, including 13 fours, as Western Australia recorded a seven-wicket win at Bellerive Oval in Hobart.
Chasing a target of 178 for victory, the visitors progressed cautiously to 180 for three in 52 overs after starting the fourth and final day of the match on 27 without loss.
The victory, worth six points, lifted Western Australia clear of New South Wales and Queensland, who share second place in the competition with 20 points.
But Western Australia's celebrations were tempered by an injury to fast bowler Brendon Julian, who strained a muscle in his side and is expected to be out of action for two weeks.
Tasmania earned two points for a first innings lead after dismissing Western Australia for 312, two runs short of their own total, earlier in the match.
Western Australia captain and all-rounder Tom Moody paved the way for the victory on Sunday when he took seven for 41 as Tasmania were dismissed 175 in their second innings.
